abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of InP on silicon is essential for the next generation of electronic systems by enabling high-performance photonics and radio frequency devices. Near-infrared Laser Lift-Off (LLO) is a promising route to enable the cost-effective transfer of InP-based device layers onto Si platforms. However, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To clarify these laser-material interactions, we investigate an InP/InGaAs heterostructure under single-pulse 1064 nm irradiation. Through microstructural characterization and coupled optical-thermal simulations, we reveal that the LLO process deviates fundamentally from the conventional sacrificial layer decomposition model. Instead, we identify an energy-dependent transition driven by highly localized transient melting and dynamic optical property changes. At moderate energies, rapid atomic intermixing and phosphorus depletion occur within a short-lived liquid phase, followed by epitaxial recrystallization that preserves macroscopic structural integrity. At higher energies, thermally induced bandgap shrinkage in the nominally transparent InP strongly enhances direct 1064 nm absorption. This initiates a positive feedback loop of thermal runaway, shifting the dominant energy absorption from the InGaAs sacrificial layer toward the InP layer and causing catastrophic ablation. These findings suggest that the onset of InP self-absorption imposes a critical high-energy constraint on the LLO process, rather than the sacrificial-layer decomposition threshold alone, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding and optimizing InP layer transfer.

title: A High-Brightness, Low-Energy-Spread Au Needle Point Electron Source Nanocold-Cathode Adapted to Low-Power Photoelectric Coexcitation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract To address the requirements of vacuum electronic and optoelectronic device applications for next-generation low-power-consumption, high-brightness, low-energy-spread, and tunable electron sources, the pursuit of high-efficiency metal nanocold-cathodes with plasmon-enhanced properties in specific waveband emerges as one of potent solutions. In this study, by screening and comparing the cathode materials and structures, we propose a high-brightness, low-energy-spread Au needle nanocold-cathode point electron source adapted to low-intensity photoelectric coexcitation. The experimental results demonstrate sensitivity to excitation light and outstanding electron emission performance of this point electron source: under the coexcitation of an electrostatic field below ∼1.25 V μm–1 and a supercontinuum-spectrum laser with average intensity of ∼24 W cm–2, the source achieved an emission current of 130 nA, improving by one order of magnitude when compared to the field emission current (∼13 nA) under pure electrostatic field excitation. As the laser excitation intensity increased, its effective work function decreased from 5.1 to 2.7 eV, resulting in a significant reduction of the excitation threshold for electron emission. Benefiting from the plasmon-enhanced light-harvesting effect, the cathode exhibits high sensitivity and selectivity to the wavelength and polarization of the incident light. In the 532–675 nm plasmon resonance band, the emission current exceeds 225 nA at an average excitation intensity of only 7.05 W cm–2, ∼17 times the pure electrostatic field emission current. Meanwhile, the plasmon relaxation preferentially populates high-energy electrons and suppresses the energy spread broadening induced by the space charge effect, thereby achieving a high reduced brightness of 6.89 × 109 A m–2 sr–1 V–1 and a low-energy spread of approximately 0.5 eV. This low-power photoelectric coexcitation scheme greatly relaxes the requirements on the excitation source, providing a route for the miniaturization and integration of vacuum optoelectronic point electron sources.

title: Amino-Terminated Ti3C2T x MXene Prepared via Ammonia Treatment Boosts Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Defect-mediated non-radiative recombination and progressive material degradation impose fundamental limits on the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and operational durability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). To address this issue, we synthesized amino-terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene (denoted as A-MXene) nanosheets through LiF/HCl etching and subsequent ammonia post-treatment and incorporated them into PSCs. Characterization results reveal that ammonia treatment modifies the surface/interlayer chemistry of Ti3C2Tx and introduces amino-related nitrogen species, accompanied by increased interlayer spacing, reduced lateral flake dimensions, and enhanced dispersibility. In PSCs, A-MXene regulates both Pb- and I-related chemical environments, improves perovskite crystallization, suppresses non-radiative recombination, and promotes interfacial hole extraction. Consequently, the A-MXene-modified device delivers a PCE of 23.49%. Moreover, the encapsulated device retains 94.9% of its initial PCE after 720 h of uninterrupted 1-sun illumination at 85 °C in a N2 atmosphere. These findings establish ammonia-treated MXene as a versatile additive capable of concurrently governing defect chemistry and charge transport, thereby enabling high-efficiency, stable PSCs.

title: Cross-Dimensional Percolation and Metastructure-Assisted Highly Efficient Electromagnetic Interference Shielding Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Increasing electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues make shielding materials urgent in need. However, designing a thin/lightweight material with high shielding effectiveness (SE over 100 dB) by facile and scalable technologies with high production accuracy is still challenging. Herein, excellent shielding composite films are successfully prepared through sequential scalable positive pressure filtration, accurate inkjet printing, and facile transferring. From mass ratio optimization of 1D silver nanowires to 2D MXene, a skeleton with maximum inner free space and fast electron and phonon transport channels through cross-dimensional percolation is produced for internal multiple reflection absorption. To further increase EMI SE, graphene-based mesh metamaterials are theoretically calculated and accurately printed with controlled conductivity for impedance matching as the top layer. Facile inkjet printing succeeds in balancing print accuracy and conductivity control by advanced ink formulation. Finally, under multiple attenuation mechanisms verified through complex permittivity analysis in both frequency domain and real space (conductive loss, dipole polarization, and various interfacial polarizations), EMI SE of 102.31 dB in X-band is achieved. Integrating different attenuation technologies in a single material system of multidimensions inspires further designing shielding materials with increasingly strict requirements like multiband compatibility with special frequency enhancement.

title: Hansen Solubility-Guided Design Optimization of Biopolymer–Drug Compatibility for Photodynamically Antimicrobial Biomaterials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Designing polymeric nanocarriers for hydrophobic therapeutics requires an understanding of polymer–drug interactions and their dependence on polymer molecular weight. Herein, poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) oligomers (αPBS) with tunable molecular weights were prepared via controlled microwave-assisted alcoholysis to investigate the relationships among molecular weight, solubility behavior, and curcumin encapsulation. Experimental solubility mapping revealed substantial deviations between experimentally determined and conventionally predicted Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) in the oligomeric regime, highlighting the limitations of group-contribution methods for low-molecular-weight polyesters. The PBS oligomer with a M̅n of approximately 2,000 g/mol (αPBS6) exhibited experimental HSP values of δD = 17.0, δP = 7.3, and δH = 7.1 MPa½. Despite borderline-to-unfavorable HSP-derived compatibility with curcumin (RED ≈ 1.04 and χ ≈ 1.21), αPBS6 exhibited high curcumin encapsulation, demonstrating that HSP-derived parameters alone do not directly predict encapsulation efficiency. Curcumin-loaded αPBS nanoparticles (Cur@PBS6) had an average diameter of 232 ± 1.5 nm, a high loading capacity (8.54–9.10%), and good colloidal stability. Their loading capacity exceeded those of commercial PBS (6.36%), PBSA (6.64%), and PLA (2.75%) systems, indicating that molecular-weight modification and nanoparticle formation conditions contribute to curcumin incorporation. Spectroscopic analyses suggested reduced curcumin aggregation following encapsulation, which preserved its photoactivity and promoted reactive oxygen species generation under blue-light irradiation. Moreover, Cur@PBS6-incorporated electrospun poly(lactic acid) fibers exhibited photodynamic antibacterial activity under blue-light irradiation (450 nm, 0.3 W/cm2, 60 min), achieving bacterial killing efficiencies of 94.2% against Escherichia coli and 98.1% against Staphylococcus aureus. These findings demonstrate that experimentally determined HSPs provide a complementary framework for evaluating molecular-weight-dependent polymer–drug interactions, while nanocarrier performance is collectively governed by molecular weight, crystallinity, formulation condition, and other physicochemical factors.

title: Manganese-Coordinated Rhein Hydrogel as a Vaccine Adjuvant for Synergistically Enhanced Humoral and Cellular Immunity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Manganese ions (Mn2+), which act as agonists of the cGAS-STING pathway, hold considerable promise as vaccine adjuvants. However, free Mn2+ is rapidly cleared after injection, making it difficult to sustain local immune stimulation. In this study, we exploited the coordination between Mn2+ and rhein, a naturally occurring anthraquinone small molecule, to construct a novel injectable Rhe@Mn hydrogel through one-step self-assembly. Within the hydrogel, densely packed supramolecular nanofibers intertwine to form a three-dimensional network, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) confirmed the uniform distribution of Mn along the nanofibers. Rheological testing showed that the Rhe@Mn hydrogel had favorable viscoelasticity and structural stability. In vitro studies, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel retained the STING-agonist activity of Mn2+ and effectively promoted antigen uptake by DCs and their maturation. In vivo, the hydrogel formed an antigen depot at the injection site, enabling sustained antigen release for up to 10 days. It also efficiently recruited immune cells, including DCs and macrophages, thereby establishing a local immune microenvironment enriched in antigen-presenting cells. After a single immunization, the Rhe@Mn hydrogel vaccine increased the abundance of germinal-center B (GC B) cells in lymph nodes by approximately 3.7-fold, significantly enhanced antigen-specific humoral and cellular immune responses, and established durable immune memory. This study provides a facile, functionally integrated platform for adjuvant-antigen co-delivery in subunit vaccines.

title: A DNA Origami Nanodevice Programs CD20 Spatial Organization for Selective Apoptosis of Malignant B Cells in Lymphoma Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triggering CD20 clustering to induce B cell apoptosis is considered a promising therapeutic strategy for dysregulated, B cell-driven diseases, yet current methods lack the spatial precision to organize CD20 into defined clusters and fail to discriminate malignant from normal B cells. Here, we describe an intelligent DNA origami nanodevice that integrates an optimized anti-CD20 antibody array with a conformational switch to selectively induce CD20 clustering and apoptosis in B-cell lymphoma. Benefiting from the nanometric precision of DNA origami, we found that arranging anti-CD20 antibodies into a pentavalent array with approximately 10 nm spacing most effectively drives CD20 clustering and downstream apoptosis. Under resting conditions, the nanodevice stays in a closed, tubular shape that conceals the antibody array inside and therefore remains harmless to normal B cells. Upon encountering c-Met expressed on lymphoma B cells, the device unrolls into a planar sheet and exposes the antibody array, triggering potent apoptotic signaling specifically in these malignant cells. In a Raji xenograft mouse model, intravenously injected nanodevices specifically unrolled at the tumor site, inhibited tumor growth by more than 70%, and produced no significant systemic toxicity. By coupling programmable ligand nanopatterning with a shape-changing switch, this DNA origami platform offers a generalizable strategy for receptor-mediated disease therapy.

title: Slide-Ring Hydrogel Networks Cross-Linked by Movable Cucurbit[8]uril/Macromer Host-Guest Complexes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract For traditional covalently cross-linked hydrogels, achieving both stiffness and toughness is generally difficult, owing to the fixed cross-linking points and the lack of dynamic response. Introducing movable cross-linking points into the network has proven to be an effective strategy to overcome this limitation. However, most existing approaches rely on pseudopolyrotaxane architectures based on cyclodextrin (CD) and polyethylene glycol (PEG), which require complicated synthesis. In this study, slide-ring hydrogels were conveniently synthesized via free radical polymerization of acrylamide (AM) and acrylic acid (AA) monomers, employing a supramolecular complex of azobenzene guest-modified telechelic macromers (Acr-Azo-PEG20K-Azo-Acr) and cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) as movable cross-linkers. Benefiting from the introduction of dynamic host–guest cross-linking, these hydrogels possess movable cross-linking points that can effectively dissipate energy and distribute stress during deformation, thereby significantly enhancing the mechanical properties through the pulley effect. By tuning the cross-linker content, solid content, and monomer structure, the material properties could be precisely optimized. Furthermore, posttreatment with ferric citrate (FeCA) allowed the introduction of Fe3+ dynamic coordination cross-linking into the acrylic-based slide-ring hydrogels, achieving a simultaneous 3-fold increase in tensile strength and an approximately 4-fold increase in toughness while maintaining high ductility and excellent fatigue resistance. The use of macromer/CB[8] complexes as movable cross-linkers offers a new strategy for high-performance hydrogels and lays a solid foundation for their future applications.

title: Microstructured Ionic Polymer-Based Multifunctional Iontronic Skin for Pressure Sensing, Object Recognition, and Underwater Environmental Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Skin-like iontronic sensors capable of multifunctional sensing and reliable operation hold strong potential for next-generation wearable electronics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and multifunctionality within a single platform remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a multifunctional iontronic skin based on a microstructured ionic polymer (MSiP) composed of PVDF and [EMIM]+[BF4]– ion pairs. The MSiP is fabricated through mask-less photolithography to create highly ordered micropillar arrays with a diameter of 30 μm, a height of 5 μm, and an interspacing of 20 μm. The iontronic skin is constructed by sandwiching the MSiP layer between flexible PDMS/PEDOT:PSS electrodes, where pressure-induced migration of highly mobile [BF4]– ions, as revealed by molecular dynamics simulations, facilitates electrical double-layer formation at the MSiP/electrode interface, resulting in enhanced capacitive response. Moreover, finite-element simulations reveal that the microstructured architecture effectively concentrates local stress, increases the effective contact area, and amplifies structural deformation during compression, thereby accounting for the exceptional pressure sensitivity of the MSiP sensor. As a result, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh pressure sensitivity of 833 kPa–1, a highly linear response (R2 = 0.98), and excellent durability over 20,000 loading–unloading cycles. Its remarkable sensitivity enables the detection of pressures as low as 3 Pa. Furthermore, integration with a robotic arm enables the development of a tactile robotic interface platform capable of real-time object grasping, lifting, and releasing in response to tactile forces applied to the sensor surface. The sensor can also be attached to the human body to monitor physiological signals and various body movements. Beyond tactile sensing, when combined with machine learning, the sensor can accurately distinguish objects ranging from soft cloth to rigid steel bottles, achieving a high classification accuracy of 95–97%. The iontronic sensor also demonstrates underwater sensing, including monitoring of depth (0–35 cm), temperature (20–80 °C), and salinity (0–8 ppt). This work presents a versatile iontronic platform that enables high-performance multifunctional sensing for wearable electronics, intelligent robotics, human–machine interfaces, and underwater environmental monitoring.

title: Integrated Droplet Microfluidic Platform for Single-Spheroid Photothermal Nanotherapy and Morphology-Driven Response Prediction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photothermal therapy (PTT) is a promising cancer treatment modality, but its evaluation remains limited by the lack of physiologically relevant and quantitatively controlled in vitro platforms. Here, we present a droplet-based microfluidic platform that enables single-spheroid formation, programmable nanoparticle delivery, and in situ laser irradiation with real-time thermal monitoring. The platform enables temperature multiplexing within a single experiment, allowing construction of single-spheroid dose–response relationships and the definition of a temperature-based inhibitory metric (IT50). This provides a direct and physically meaningful quantification of photothermal efficacy. In parallel, a label-free, spheroid morphology-based machine learning approach predicts treatment response across cell types, nanoparticle incubation conditions, and therapeutic regimes while preserving intrinsic single-spheroid variability. Despite a limited dataset size and biological heterogeneity, the system achieves robust and reproducible predictive performance. Overall, this work establishes a scalable and versatile microfluidic framework for quantitative photothermal nanotherapy screening, integrating controlled thermal dosing, 3D tumor models, and morphological data-driven analysis within a single-spheroid platform.

title: Architecting Co-continuous PVDF Composites via Multi-material 3D Parallel Printing for Enhanced Piezoelectricity and Wearable Sensing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoelectric composites have attracted considerable attention for self-powered sensing; however, achieving efficient electromechanical response while maintaining structural integrity under repeated deformation remains challenging. Herein, a structure-driven multi-material 3D parallel printing strategy is developed to construct polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based piezoelectric composites with a co-continuous dual-phase architecture. In this design, ionic liquid (IL)-modified PVDF serves as the piezoelectric phase, where the IL promotes β-phase formation and dipole orientation, while carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-reinforced PVDF provides a conductive phase for electrical signal collection. Unlike conventional stacked configurations, the parallel-printed architecture enables continuous integration of the piezoelectric and conductive phases, providing intimate interfacial contact and a mechanically interconnected structure. The resulting structural continuity facilitates stress transfer during mechanical deformation and contributes to a stable electromechanical response. Kelvin probe force microscopy measurements further reveal an interfacial potential difference of 85.6 mV, indicating distinct interfacial electrical characteristics between the two phases. The optimized sensor delivers an output voltage of 0.55 V at 5 N, a sensitivity of 439.77 mV/N in the low-force regime, and a response time of 28 ms, together with excellent mechanical stability. Finite element analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced piezoelectric response is closely associated with the continuous deformation and effective stress transfer enabled by the parallel architecture. The sensor further exhibits reliable performance in human-motion monitoring and human–machine interaction. This work establishes multi-material 3D parallel printing as a structure-engineering approach for integrating piezoelectric and conductive phases and provides a versatile route toward high-performance flexible piezoelectric sensing devices.

title: Enhanced Performance of Protonic Ceramic Electrolysis Cells via Transient Sinterlayer Engineering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Protonic ceramic electrolysis cells (PCECs) are a promising technology for efficient hydrogen production at intermediate temperatures (500–600 °C), but their commercialization is hindered by fabrication challenges. In particular, the high-temperature sintering required to densify barium cerate–zirconate electrolytes promotes barium volatilization, leading to phase decomposition and degraded performance. Here, we introduce a transient sinterlayer processing strategy in which a thin (∼1 μm) surface coating is applied atop the electrolyte before sintering. During high-temperature processing, the sinterlayer suppresses electrolyte decomposition, promotes densification and grain growth, and is ultimately incorporated into the perovskite lattice, yielding a chemically uniform perovskite electrolyte. Three sinterlayer compositions (CeO2, La2O3, and La2Ce2O7) were evaluated for BaCe0.7Zr0.1Y0.1Yb0.1O3–δ electrolytes. La2O3 provided the greatest benefit by enhancing grain growth, preserving dopant distributions, and substantially improving stability upon exposure to boiling water, although degradation under CO2-containing conditions at 550 °C remained evident. Integrated into complete electrolysis cells, La2O3 sinterlayers increased current density by 67.2% at 1.3 V and 600 °C while improving Faradaic efficiency from 78.8 to 85.0% relative to a bare cell. These results establish transient sinterlayers as an effective fabrication strategy for high-performance PCECs.

title: Prepressed Liquid Metal Fabric with Strain-Insensitive Conductance for Wearable Bioelectronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of flexible conductors with high electrical conductivity, flexibility, and electromechanical stability is important for reliable signal transmission in wearable electronics. Here, we report a patternable liquid metal (LM) fabric with strain-insensitive performance, fabricated using a highly elastic knitted fabric (KF) as the substrate and a gallium-based liquid metal as the conductive coating. A patterned poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) intermediate layer was introduced to enhance the interfacial adhesion and facilitate the selective deposition of LM on the textile substrate. In addition, pre‑oxidation of the LM followed by a prepressing treatment further promotes the permeation of liquid metal into the knitted fabric, thereby improving the stability of electrical conductivity. Benefiting from the pore structure of the fabric and the strong interfacial combination of liquid metal and PEDOT:PSS, this composite fabric achieves a strain capacity of 200% with low resistance variations, and the resistance change rates are 18.6% for longitudinal stretching, 20.4% for 45° diagonal stretching, and 24.8% for transverse stretching. When stretched by 100% along three distinct directions (transverse, longitudinal, and 45°), the resistance change rate remains below 5% in all cases, demonstrating excellent multidirectional strain-insensitive conductivity. Moreover, after 1000 cyclic stretching cycles under a 30% strain, the resistance fluctuation still stays within 3%. The resulting fabric exhibited excellent conductivity stability when applied to conductors, Joule heating, electrocardiogram (ECG), and near field communication (NFC), demonstrating its potential for next‑generation wearable electronics.

title: From gas generation to intelligent management: a gas-signal-driven framework for thermal runaway early warning in lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Thermal runaway (TR) in lithium-ion batteries poses a critical challenge to the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems. Conventional battery management systems (BMSs), which primarily rely on voltage and temperature signals, frequently exhibit delayed response and limited capability for early-stage fault detection. Gas signals, generated at the early stages of TR, provide rich physicochemical information on internal reactions and offer unique potential for timely warning and fault diagnosis. This review presents a gas-signal-driven early warning framework that systematically integrates mechanism understanding, signal sensing, and intelligent decision-making. The framework is designed to upgrade current BMS architectures without major hardware redesign. Specifically, this review (i) deconstructs multi-stage gas generation mechanisms, characteristic gas fingerprints across different battery chemistries, and their spatiotemporal evolution; (ii) critically evaluates state-of-the-art gas sensing technologies and their applicability to practical battery systems; and (iii) synthesizes intelligent early warning architectures, with an emphasis on multi-sensor fusion and AI-based methods to enhance detection reliability, extend warning lead time, and enable predictive safety interventions. In addition, key engineering challenges-including trace gas detection under realistic conditions, environmental interference, long-term sensor stability, and constraints for edge deployment-are systematically discussed. Future directions toward cloud-edge collaboration are also outlined. Beyond early warning, this infrastructure also holds promise for full-lifecycle management, including state estimation and maintenance scheduling.

title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

title: Nanostructure-Enabled Apparent Slip through Dynamic Hydration Reorganization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dynamic transport across solid–liquid nanointerfaces is commonly interpreted through equilibrium wettability, although increasing evidence suggests that interfacial hydration rather than contact angle governs nanoscale liquid motion. However, how hydration reorganizes under ionic and hydrodynamic perturbations at strongly hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that dendritic silica nanostructures create a hydration-rich interphase whose dynamic mechanical state can be programmed by electrolyte concentration, flow, and biomolecular adsorption. Contact-angle measurements, density functional theory calculations, and overtone-resolved quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring reveal that intermediate ionic strengths maximize near-surface acoustic loading without a proportional increase in dissipation, while increasing flow induces a flow-dependent enhancement in model-derived apparent mobility. The response is strongest at higher overtones and persists after bovine serum albumin adsorption, demonstrating that the adaptive hydration state survives the formation of a complex protein–water interphase. Rather than reflecting the classical hydrophobic slip, the observations identify a dynamically reconfigurable hydration layer that decouples equilibrium wettability from interfacial mechanics. These findings establish hydration-layer reconfigurability as a general mechanism governing liquid mobility at hydrophilic nanostructured interfaces and provide a design framework for nanofluidic transport, antifouling materials, separation membranes, and interfacial biosensing technologies.

title: Ultrasonic metamaterial at MHz frequencies using microstructured glass
abstract: Acoustic metamaterials enhance traditional material properties, providing opportunities to shape sound fields in applications ranging from biomedical imaging and clinical therapy to nondestructive testing. However, at the megahertz frequency range, only a few metamaterial architectures exist. They are often highly attenuating or difficult to manufacture and generally provide limited control. Here, we introduce a megahertz-frequency ultrasonic metamaterial based on laser-engraved glass. By structuring metavoxels with different engraving patterns, we define an anisotropic metamaterial exhibiting local variations in the sound speed of up to 20% compared to unstructured glass and losses 100× lower than in comparable three-dimensional–printed metamaterials. We use this metamaterial to define a library of standard elements that can be modularly combined to shape complex-patterned ultrasonic fields. Our experiments are supported by a theoretical model, which provides additional insights into the microstructural origin of the metamaterial behavior and opens the door to designing tailored ultrasound fields and responses.

title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Jahn–Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn–N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn–N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2–y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

title: In situ processing of fibrous hydrogels by photochemistry for adaptive cellular microenvironments
abstract: Omnipresent in biology, fibrous networks like collagen possess unique properties: dynamic network via crosslinking and degradation. This intrinsic adaptivity plays a critical role in regulating cell behavior via cell-matrix interactions. Built from biological building blocks, however, these networks are challenging to manipulate or even control. Here, we introduce dynamic network regulation via photochemical control in a synthetic and fibrous highly biomimetic hydrogel. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate that the dynamic control over the mechanical properties of this adaptive in vitro model can be used to modulate cell spreading and mechanotransduction in three-dimensional (3D) mesenchymal stromal cell cultures. Our approach not only opens the door to on-demand mechanically adaptive gels with unprecedented control, but simultaneously offers easy processibility and cell extraction of the used synthetic gel.

title: CCAN forms the spherical shell-like structure in interphase kinetochores
abstract: The kinetochore is an essential structure for the faithful chromosome segregation during mitosis. The 16-protein complex known as the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN) localizes the centromere throughout the cell cycle and forms the basis of the kinetochore. Although cryo–electron microscopy has provided a structural model of an individual CCAN unit, how multiple CCAN units are organized within cells remains unclear. Here, using in silico and in vivo analyses, we demonstrate that multiple CCAN units form a spherical shell-like structure in interphase DT40 kinetochores. CENP-T and CENP-N localize to the CCAN shell, whereas the CENP-C cupin domain clusters at the center. Molecular dynamics simulations of CCAN assembly suggest that CENP-C–DNA interactions constrain the orientation of CCAN units, supporting a spherical shell-like organization via CENP-C oligomerization. Super-resolution imaging reveals the spherical shell-like structure at DT40 kinetochores, and CENP-C knockout or expression of a CENP-C DNA binding deficient mutant abolishes the structure, consistent with the simulation-derived model. These findings provide important insights into the spatial organization of functional kinetochores within cells.

title: Staphylococcus aureus wall teichoic acid structure dictates virulence potential and resistance to host defenses
abstract:
Staphylococcus aureus
                    is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved
                    sasF
                    gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when
                    S. aureus
                    colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for
                    S. aureus
                    resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of
                    sasF
                    are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper
                    S. aureus
                    surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
abstract:
Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ
                    p
                     = 10.42 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    , μ
                    n
                     = 30.23 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml
                    −1
                    for
                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

title: Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO 2
abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide—a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits
abstract:
The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice,
                    Dmrt1
                    −/−
                    females are fertile, although they show a reduction of
                    Stra8
                    expression. Using our
                    DMRT1
                    mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation when
                    DMRT1
                    expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development,
                    DMRT1
                    −/−
                    gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.

title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer’s disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2–magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer–MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation
abstract:
Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of
                    Plasmodium
                    parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of
                    Plasmodium vivax
                    (
                    P. vivax
                    ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of
                    P. vivax
                    merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent
                    P. vivax
                    merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized
                    P. vivax
                    merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N 2 O 5 hydrolysis
abstract:
Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

title: A phosphorylation-gated GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 module controls drought-responsive transcription
abstract:
Drought adaptation requires rapid spatial reorganization of signaling proteins to reprogram stress-responsive transcription, yet how phosphorylation coordinates this process remains unclear. Here we aimed to define how phosphorylation-gated protein relocalization regulates a BpLBD1-centered drought pathway in
                    Betula platyphylla
                    (birch). Drought activated two kinase branches: BpAGC phosphorylated BpMAPK6 at Ser318 within a cryptic nuclear localization signal, promoting importin α recognition, whereas BpCKII phosphorylated BpGAPDH at Thr109, Thr270, Ser279 and Thr298, promoting importin β recognition. Dual phosphorylation enabled coordinated nuclear accumulation of BpMAPK6 and BpGAPDH. In the nucleus, phosphorylated BpGAPDH acted as a scaffold-like adaptor coupling BpMAPK6 to BpLBD1, enabling BpMAPK6-mediated phosphorylation of BpLBD1 at Ser29. This weakened BpLBD1 binding to the
                    BpMYB123
                    promoter, reduced expression of the drought-sensitivity regulator
                    BpMYB123
                    , and de-repressed drought-responsive genes such as
                    BpRD29B
                    . Disrupting
                    BpGAPDH
                    or BpLBD1 Ser29 phosphorylation compromised drought tolerance. Thus, a phospho-spatial GAPDH-MAPK6-LBD1 switch couples nuclear protein assembly to drought-responsive transcription.

title: CREBBP loss drives immune evasion by epigenetically silencing STING and MHC-I in small cell lung cancer
abstract:
Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify
                    CREBBP
                    loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in
                    Rb1/Trp53
                    -driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently,
                    Crebbp
                    deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically,
                    Crebbp
                    loss suppresses
                    Sting
                    and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both
                    Crebbp
                    -mutant and
                    Crebbp
                    -wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in
                    Crebbp
                    -mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish
                    CREBBP
                    loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

title: Physical confinement modulates the rate-limiting transition in the release of phosphate from actin filaments
abstract:
The nucleotide state and rates of transitions between states regulate the dynamics of ATPases. Slow inorganic phosphate (P
                    i
                    ) release following ATP hydrolysis is often rate limiting and associated with key conformational changes. Actin filaments offer a unique opportunity to understand the fundamentals of P
                    i
                    release because identical subunits at filament ends and the interior release P
                    i
                    at markedly different rates. The molecular origin of this difference is debated, so we used extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize P
                    i
                    release from different subunits within an actin filament. The calculated dissociation rates of P
                    i
                    from ADP-Mg
                    2+
                    in the active site correlate with experimentally measured P
                    i
                    release rates and scale inversely with the numbers of water molecules in the cavity surrounding the γ-phosphate. Simulations show that egress of P
                    i
                    through the protein channels, including through the N111-R177 backdoor, is not rate limiting and that subunits at the filament ends use alternative egress pathways.

title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface
abstract:
The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning–based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector
                    Anopheles coluzzii
                    in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the
                    orco
                    and
                    IR76b
                    chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between
                    An. coluzzii
                    and
                    Aedes aegypti
                    linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

title: Enterococcus faecalis biofilm rewires neutrophil metabolism to suppress antimicrobial activity
abstract:
Enterococcus faecalis
                    is an opportunistic pathogen that persists in biofilm-associated infections despite robust neutrophil recruitment. How
                    E. faecalis
                    evades neutrophils remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how
                    E. faecalis
                    biofilms alter effector functions in human neutrophils and a murine wound infection model. We found that
                    E. faecalis
                    biofilm suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, bacterial engulfment, and neutrophil-mediated control of biofilm growth. This suppression is partly driven by production of lactic acid through the lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) of
                    E. faecalis
                    , which acidifies the extracellular environment, lowers neutrophil intracellular pH, and disrupts glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway. In a murine wound infection model, loss of LDH increased neutrophil recruitment and NETosis
                    .
                    We also found that high bacterial density, a defining feature of biofilms, suppresses NETosis through a lactic acid–independent mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify biofilm immune evasion strategies mediated by bacterial metabolism and the high-density structural organization of biofilm-associated bacteria.

title: Building digital pregnancies from the single cell up
abstract: Single-cell digital twins connect in vitro drug screening studies with clinical outcomes, providing a new framework to evaluate therapies and advance precision medicine in pregnancy.

title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
abstract:
Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4
                    +
                    T cells.

title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

title: Ocean carbon sequestration during glacial climates due to combined Antarctic sea ice expansion and ocean circulation change
abstract: Glacial-interglacial transitions punctuate Earth’s Quaternary climate, accompanied by substantial atmospheric carbon dioxide and ocean carbon storage changes. The cause of atmospheric carbon drawdown during glaciations is uncertain, involving many mechanisms whose interactions are poorly understood. Here, we show that the combined expansion of Antarctic sea ice and associated changes in the meridional overturning efficiently sequester carbon in the ocean abyss, leading to a decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide. In contrast, changes in sea ice and circulation individually result in ocean carbon dioxide outgassing. When sea ice expansion and circulation changes act together, they enhance biological carbon storage by reducing ocean-atmosphere fluxes in the Southern Ocean, without invoking external drivers of the biological pump. This reduction inhibits the outgassing of upwelled remineralized carbon and promotes its resubduction into the abyss. Together, these results reveal a reinforcing feedback linking atmospheric cooling, Antarctic sea ice expansion, and ocean circulation changes to enhanced biological carbon storage and atmospheric carbon dioxide drawdown.

title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

title: RanGAP1 coordinates the ER-lamina interface to drive de novo nuclear envelope reassembly in mouse embryos
abstract:
Nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly is essential for the zygote-to-totipotency transition in mammalian embryos. Beyond its classical roles in nuclear transport and maintenance of the RanGTP gradient, the function of RanGAP1 in embryonic NE reassembly has remained elusive. Here, we show that RanGAP1 localizes to the early embryonic NE, driving reassembly via a distinct structural mechanism. Trim-Away–mediated RanGAP1 depletion causes two-cell stage arrest and severe NE defects, including nuclear pore complex (NPC) loss, failed reassembly, and aberrant “fishnet” membrane structures. Mechanistically, RanGAP1 establishes a structural paradigm for endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–lamina coupling by recruiting Lamin A/C, B1, and B2 to the ER for coassembly. The acidic domain and SUMO-1 modification at Lys
                    526
                    (K526) are essential for the NPC localization of RanGAP1. Thus, RanGAP1 orchestrates nuclear lamina (NL) assembly by targeting lamins to the ER. These findings uncover mechanisms of NE reassembly that are critical for early embryogenesis and provide insights into NE-related developmental disorders.

title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

title: Type-III Porous Liquid ZIF-8/Perfluorodecalin for O2 Delivery and CO2 Removal: Stability, Sorption, and Transport Monitored by In Situ EPR Spectroscopy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perfluorodecalin (C10F18) is a well-known gas carrier for chemical and biomedical applications. Being an inert and stable liquid, it is capable of dissolving and releasing large volumes of O2 and CO2. In this work, we propose a route for enhancing its functional properties furthermore by designing a type-III porous liquid (PL) composed of C10F18 and metal–organic framework ZIF-8. Using spin probes encapsulated in ZIF-8, we employ in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy to investigate the stability of this PL and the adsorption, transport, and desorption of O2 and CO2 in practical conditions. The prototypical flow system with EPR detection was designed to demonstrate the controllable sorption cycles of ZIF-8/C10F18 PL. The exceptional stability and appealing functional properties of this PL pave the way for its future chemical and biomedical applications.

title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4 + T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4
                    +
                    responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4
                    +
                    response was strongly T helper 1 (T
                    H
                    1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T
                    H
                    2 cytokines. Both CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

title: C–C Bond Formation via the Addition or Redistribution of Hydrogen: Chemical Synthesis Beyond Premetalated Reagents or Metallic Reductants
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stoichiometric organometallic reagents are used in countless C–C bond-forming processes but are often hazardous, display poor functional group compatibility, and require multistep preparation from the parent platform chemicals. Zerovalent metals are also used to mediate reductive C–C bond formation, but their use at scale poses similar safety and engineering concerns. The formation of C-nucleophiles as transient catalytic intermediates via hydrogen transfer from abundant low-molecular-weight reductants (H2, Me2CHOH, HCO2H) offers a more ideal alternative to preformed carbanions or zerovalent metals in reductive C–C bond formation. Related hydrogen autotransfer processes where reactants serve as redox pairs en route to products of C–C coupling also are desirable, as they avoid both sacrificial reductants and premetalated reagents. In this Review, hydrogen-mediated variants of classical reactions that exploit carbanions or zerovalent metals are described.

title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
abstract:
Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3:
                    K

                    K
                    d
                     = 24.0 ± 3.3 μM, τ = 537 ± 22 seconds) and cortisol (Cy3:
                    K

                     = 36.6 ± 3.9 μM, τ = 205 ± 7 seconds; Cy5:

                     = 30.7 ± 5.5 μM, τ = 259 ± 4 seconds) in buffer, serum, and artificial cerebrospinal fluid. Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

title: Prioritizing reducing impacts on species to minimize residual reserves
abstract: International conservation goals have driven rapid expansion of protected areas. This growth has favored quantity over quality, and often results in residual reserves (i.e., areas where species already experience minimal anthropogenic impact). Spatial prioritization is commonly used to help design protected area networks that represent species while minimizing costs to stakeholders. This approach can result in the siting of protected areas that do not decrease impacts on species of conservation concern. Here, we show how measures of cumulative impacts on species can be used in a spatial prioritization to site protected areas to reduce impacts on species of conservation concern. We use a trait-based vulnerability framework and anthropogenic stressor maps to quantify cumulative impacts from four human activities, and incorporate those impacts into spatial prioritizations. We demonstrate that the inclusion of cumulative impacts on species in spatial prioritization can more efficiently protect biodiversity, balance socioeconomic objectives, and avoid residual reserve outcomes.

title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.

title: Wave vortices around oscillating subwavelength holes: Water-wave observation
abstract: We consider a two-dimensional wave system containing a subwavelength hole, such as an aperture in an interface supporting surface electromagnetic or acoustic waves or an island in a fluid surface sustaining gravity-capillary waves. Recent studies have revealed the emergence of pronounced wave vortices around such structures, termed type II vortices, in contrast to conventional (type I) vortices associated with phase singularities and intensity nulls. A notable natural manifestation of type II vortices occurs in ocean tides around islands such as New Zealand, Madagascar, and Iceland, where the tidal phase increases by ±2π around the island. Although this phenomenon is usually associated with the Coriolis effect from the rotation of the Earth, here, we demonstrate the controlled generation of type II vortices using a minimal and tunable setup: a dipole-oscillating subwavelength hole and a single incident plane wave. Using laboratory gravity-capillary waves and an oscillating subwavelength “island,” we directly measure the resulting phase structure, topological charge, and wave angular momentum. We show that the emergence and handedness of the vortices can be precisely controlled via the relative phase between the dipolar source and the incident wave. Our results offer a simple and versatile mechanism for engineering subwavelength wave vortices, with potential applications in a variety of two-dimensional wave systems.

title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

title: p75 NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
abstract:
The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75
                    NTR
                    ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis.
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75
                    NTR
                    axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    expression levels. Together, these data establish p75
                    NTR
                    as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75
                    NTR
                    axis as a potential therapeutic target.

abstract:
A continuous transition between phases hosting distinct excitations—bosonic magnons versus fermionic spinons—is a long-sought phenomenon in quantum magnetism, analogous to the confinement-deconfinement transition in quantum chromodynamics.
