title: Unveiling the role of crystallinity of RuO2 catalysts for regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction
abstract: The intrinsic role of crystallinity in regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on RuO2 remains elusive due to the synthetic challenge of decoupling structural order from compositional variations. Here, we develop an oxygen-partial-pressure-controlled pyrolysis strategy to achieve graded crystallinity in pure RuO2 nanocatalysts, establishing a pristine model to elucidate this structure-function relationship. We reveal that amorphous RuO2 features disordered dangling oxygen that readily undergoes protonation, triggering a rapid but degradative lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM) with an ultralow overpotential of 154 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Conversely, increasing crystallinity stabilizes the RuO6 framework, suppressing protonation and shifting the pathway toward the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM). Crucially, highly crystalline RuO2 demands excessive cell voltages (1.72 V at 1.0 A cm−2) in proton exchange membrane electrolyzers, paradoxically accelerating oxidative etching. This work uncovers a crystallinity-driven LOM-to-AEM transition, identifying intermediate crystallinity as a practical strategy for balancing activity and stability.

title: Two pathways driving Phanerozoic temperature change: low-latitude radiative forcing and outgassing-weathering-vegetation carbon feedbacks
abstract: Two potentially interacting pathways may have shaped Phanerozoic temperature change: radiative effects linked to low-latitude land area and carbon-cycle feedbacks involving volcanic outgassing, silicate weathering, and terrestrial organic-carbon burial. Together, these processes provide a framework for understanding long-term climate evolution over the past 540 million years.

title: A Geometrically Tunable Cardiovascular Shunt for the Individualized Care of Neonates with Congenital Heart Defects
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Congenital heart defects (CHDs), particularly single-ventricle anomalies such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), require early surgical intervention using fixed-diameter vascular shunts. However, current shunts are incapable of adapting to the physiological changes of infant growth, often leading to hemodynamic imbalance and elevated mortality risk. Here, we report a geometrically tunable cardiovascular shunt lined with a photoresponsive hydrogel based on methacrylated dextran (DexMA) and dithiothreitol (DTT). This dual-stage crosslinked hydrogel system enables minimally invasive modulation of the inner lumen diameter in response to external blue light. We optimized the hydrogel composition to achieve both mechanical robustness (Young’s modulus ≈ 8.5 kPa) and light-induced deswelling, allowing for lumen expansion up to 39% with high stability over one month. In vitro studies confirmed excellent cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and minimal immune activation. Prototype annular shunts demonstrated precise, programmable diameter increases (15–18%) corresponding to computational models of infant growth. This dynamic, photoresponsive platform is a critical advance toward implantable materials for personalized cardiovascular interventions and a significant step toward growth-accommodating pediatric medical devices.

title: A Full-Duplex Metasurface for Simultaneous and Independent Control of Radiation and Reflection
abstract: Metasurfaces have transformed electromagnetic interfaces from fixed, material-defined boundaries into engineered platforms for tailoring wave propagation, spanning both passive designs and actively programmable implementations. For future information systems, a central challenge is to make the same physical aperture operate simultaneously as a radiating antenna and a reconfigurable reflector. Radiation–reflection-integrated (R2I) metasurfaces combine these functions, but their responses remain coupled: configuring the surface for radiation constrains its behavior in reflection. They therefore cannot generally provide independent operation at the same time, frequency, and polarization. Here, we show an intelligent full-duplex R2I metasurface that overcomes this constraint. The surface integrates controllable meta-atoms with a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW). Because the SIW-guided and free-space excitations occupy largely separated regions of the spatial spectrum, the radiated and reflected fields can be manipulated simultaneously and independently on the same aperture. We experimentally demonstrate this capability in integrated sensing and communication and in integrated detection and stealth, both realized using a single artificial-intelligence-assisted metasurface under identical operating conditions. These results establish a route towards full-duplex, single-aperture information systems.

title: Metastable synchronization and inertial-beating sensing in nonlinear oscillators
abstract: Synchronization is widely used to enhance the sensitivity and noise resilience of mechanical sensors, while nonlinear operation is often assumed to substantially broaden the usable synchronization bandwidth. Here, we show that this apparent bandwidth enhancement is fundamentally metastable. In nonlinear self-oscillating systems, large portions of the nominal synchronization region are dynamically inaccessible under direct signal injection, despite being theoretically stable. We demonstrate that this breakdown originates from phase inertia, which endows phase evolution with an effective second-order response and creates inertial barriers to phase capture. As a result, nonlinear synchronization splits into a narrow dynamically accessible locking region and a much larger metastable regime in which stable phase locking exists in principle but cannot be reached in practice. Rather than suppressing this inertial unlocking behavior, we exploit it as a sensing mechanism. Near the inaccessible locking boundary, phase inertia sustains slow beating dynamics that continuously encode frequency detuning while intrinsically averaging fast phase fluctuations. The resulting inertial-beating transduction produces a continuous, history-independent sensing response and enables faster synchronization dynamics beyond the conventional locking regime. More broadly, our results reveal that synchronization bandwidth is fundamentally governed by dynamical accessibility rather than static stability, establishing phase inertia as a general organizing principle for nonlinear synchronization dynamics across driven oscillatory systems.

title: The Evolution of Brain-Computer Interfaces Towards Collaborative Intelligence
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are evolving from unidirectional control toward deeper integration of biological and machine intelligence. This transition is constrained by two complementary bottlenecks: Intent Mismatch, or Brain-to-Machine Underreach, in which user intentions cannot be sufficiently decoded, represented, or executed by the machine; and State Mismatch, or Machine-to-Brain Overload, in which system demands exceed the user’s current cognitive, affective, or neural resources. This review uses these two mismatches as an organizing framework for examining the evolution of BCIs toward brain-machine collaborative intelligence, while distinguishing non-invasive and invasive modalities according to their signal characteristics and translational constraints. We review neural decoding, generative artificial intelligence, and shared control as approaches for reducing Intent Mismatch, and passive BCIs, adaptive interaction, neurofeedback, and neuromodulation as approaches for reducing State Mismatch. By integrating these solution paths, this review outlines a pathway toward adaptive, bidirectional, and human-centered BCI systems.

title: Preconstructed Electrolyte Interphase Enables Stable Commercial V2O5 Cathodes for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) show great potential for large-scale energy storage on account of their exceptional safety, low cost, and environmental friendliness. As a representative cathode for AZIBs, commercial vanadium pentoxide (c-V2O5) still suffers from critical bottlenecks including severe vanadium dissolution, sluggish Zn2+ diffusion, and intensive interfacial side reactions in aqueous electrolytes. Herein, a novel electrochemical pretreatment strategy is developed to in-situ construct a uniform, compact ∼3 nm amorphous electrolyte interfacial layer (EIL) with an organic–inorganic composite structure on the surface of c-V2O5 in an organic lithium-ion battery system, which breaks through the limitations of unstable and inhomogeneous interfacial layers formed in conventional aqueous systems. The EIL exerts multifunctional effects by suppressing vanadium dissolution, accelerating ion diffusion, and inhibiting side reactions, endowing the modified electrode with a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.3%, outstanding cycling stability (180 mAh g–1 after 5000 cycles at a current density of 1 A g–1), and enhanced rate capability. This work could provide guidance for optimizing cathode materials of AZIBs through rational electrolyte interface engineering in the future.

title: Tailoring Viscoelasticity by Carbon Filler Dimensionality toward High-Impact-Resistant Polydiborosiloxane Composites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of lightweight and flexible materials with high-impact-resistant performance remains a critical challenge under dynamic loading conditions, including precision instruments, electronics, and military defense systems. Herein, carbon fillers with distinct dimensionality are incorporated into polydiborosiloxane (PDBS) to construct composites with tunable viscoelastic behavior and excellent impact resistance. Increasing filler dimensionality not only retains the specific shear-stiffening viscoelastic behavior of PDBS but also significantly enhances the energy-dissipation capability and impact-resistant performance of the composites. Notably, the composite with large-size graphene achieves a high impact-force attenuation rate of 92.2% under low strain-rate impact while maintaining a strength of 48.8 MPa and a toughness of 24.2 MJ/m3 under high strain-rate impact. This work highlights the critical role of filler dimensionality in tailoring the viscoelasticity toward high-impact-resistant composite materials, thereby offering potential for efficient protection under dynamic loading conditions.

title: Quantifying Sodium Metal SEI Dissolution and Relation to Corrosion Using Quartz Crystal Microbalance
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.

title: Hot Carrier Cooling Dynamics in Tin Tri-Iodide Perovskites Thin Films
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.

title: Nickel crossover builds single-atom catalysts
abstract: An article in Advanced Materials demonstrates that nickel single-atom catalysts can be formed in situ within a CO2 electrolyser, achieving nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency towards CO.

title: When microplastics become chemically active
abstract: An article in Nature shows that common microplastics are not merely passive contaminants: when immersed in water they spontaneously generate reactive oxygen species, revealing a physicochemical mechanism that may contribute to microplastic toxicity.

title: Weak-Solvating Carboxylate Ester Electrolyte Enables Hybrid Interphase via Cooperative Additives toward Wide-Temperature Sodium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.

title: A thin carbon membrane to capture carbon
abstract: Anthropogenic emissions are rapidly increasing atmospheric CO2 levels, with severe consequences for the global climate. Researchers have developed a carbon membrane as thin as only two molecular layers that sieves and captures CO2 with very high flux and selectivity, holding promise for climate change mitigation technologies.

title: Recyclable flow battery chemistry
abstract: Turning water-based flow batteries into a truly sustainable technology hinges on recycling the organic molecules inside the battery. A redox-active organic molecule has now been developed that not only outperforms the industry-standard vanadium benchmark but also offers exceptional reusability.

title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
abstract: Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance.

title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
abstract: Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO2 separation.

title: Climate warming boosts frequency and intensity of southern Africa’s rainfall extremes
abstract: Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone (a major source of rainfall across southern Africa) can trigger devastating floods. Climate-model projections indicate that these swings might occur twice as often in the twenty-first century as in the previous century and produce more intense rainfall, owing to an increased land–sea temperature contrast and poleward intensification of atmospheric circulation.

title: Bubble-Guided Self-Healing Superhydrophobic Surfaces with Dual-Mode In Situ Visual Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Superhydrophobic surfaces exhibit great application potential ranging from sophisticated droplet manipulation to aerospace and other fields, owing to their unique properties such as liquid repellent, anti-corrosion, anti-icing, drag reduction, and so on. However, maintaining the stability of the solid–liquid interface remains a major challenge: the instability of the three-phase line caused by the collapse of the air layer during dynamic transport and the degradation of surface function caused by the retention of micro–nano contaminants seriously undermine its durability. In nature, rice leaves possess oriented microgroove architectures for unidirectional droplet transport, while submerged photosynthetic plants continuously generate bubbles to sustain intact solid–air–liquid (SAL) composite layers. Inspired by these merits, we propose a directional confinement–transport strategy, in which the microcolumn structure achieves dynamic compensation of the interfacial air layer through precise submillimeter bubble manipulation and establishes a cooperative stabilization of “structural confinement–air self-replenishment”. The surface demonstrates exceptional self-cleaning and no loss transport behaviors, vastly expanding its applicability in extreme environments. In addition, we construct a monitoring system based on interfacial chemical reactions, which enables in situ visual monitoring of the surface wetting state and can restore its superhydrophobicity on demand. In essence, this approach not only benefits the development of the superhydrophobic field, but also provides valuable theoretical foundations and practical guidance for constructing multifunctional stable interfaces, thereby propelling the field toward practical applications.

title: Synergistic Effects of Thermally Engineered Defect-Rich Structures in Renewable Nanocarbons for Enhanced Electrochemical Performance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical performance of conventional hard carbons remains constrained by their limited surface activity and insufficient interlayer spacing for efficient sodium storage. Here, we report a microstructurally engineered carbon derived from waste passenger tyres, exhibiting tunable defect density, interlayer spacing, and pore distribution through controlled carbonization between 700 and 1500 °C. The thermally driven reconstruction of sp2/sp3 domains induces a hierarchical framework featuring short-range ordered graphene nanodomains embedded within disordered carbon matrices, generating abundant closed and open pores that synergistically facilitate ion transport and adsorption. The optimized carbon produced at 1300 °C delivers a first-cycle reversible capacity of approximately 282.1 mAhg–1, retains approximately 278.5 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles at 10 mA g–1, and exhibits sustained high-current cycling stability over 500 cycles. Detailed micromechanistic analysis reveals that the enhanced sodium storage originates from the coupling of enlarged interlayer spacing (≈0.38–0.40 nm) and optimized Raman-active disorder with the internal pore architecture, enabling coexisting diffusion-controlled intercalation and surface-induced capacitive processes. This work establishes a framework for defect-controlled microstructural engineering of tyre-derived carbons, providing mechanistic insight into the pore–defect–graphite interplay and offering a sustainable pathway for converting end-of-life rubber waste into high-performance anode materials for next-generation sodium-ion batteries.

title: I’m expected to work excessive hours in the lab. Should I speak up about my disability?
abstract: What can a researcher in an overworked laboratory do to take care of themselves and their lab-mates, and how should they navigate medical disclosure?
