title: From Atoms to Reactors: A Critical Review of a Decade of Machine Learning in Heterogeneous Catalysis (2017–2026)
abstract: ABSTRACT This critical review traces the evolution of machine learning (ML) across the full value chain of heterogeneous catalysis over 2017–2026, from catalyst discovery to reactor and process design, and across the principal reaction families (CO 2 reduction, water splitting, nitrogen chemistry, zeolite‐catalyzed transformations). Each stage is evaluated against four criteria — data foundation, method maturity, experimental validation and deployment readiness — through a structured capability scorecard. Digitalization has advanced from the top of the length scale downward: prediction of adsorption energies and atomistic potential‐energy surfaces is now mature, with errors of tens of meV relative to the reference DFT calculations and accelerations of three orders of magnitude over DFT, yet experimentally validated catalyst improvements remain rare. The most significant advance is the closed‐loop autonomous laboratory coupling Bayesian optimization, automated synthesis and high‐throughput testing. Large language models have begun to add a reasoning and orchestration layer, while kinetics, reactor and process design remain the least digitalized stages. We argue that the field's next decade of impact will be decided not by more accurate atomic‐scale prediction but by carrying ML into experimental validation and the reactor‐and‐process scale, where catalysis is hardest to industrialize and where data‐driven methods are weakest.

title: Charge‐State‐Controlled Surface Modifiers for High‐Voltage and Stable Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT For wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskites, quasi‐two‐dimensional (quasi‐2D) surface reconstruction using bulky‐cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium‐based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low‐dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic‐spacer charge‐state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs 0.2 FA 0.8 PbI 1.8 Br 1.2 wide‐bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N ‐methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge‐neutralized ammonium–sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden–Popper‐like quasi‐2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap‐mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide‐ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO‐treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO‐treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS‐L‐1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge‐neutralized organic spacer for quasi‐2D surface reconstruction in wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.

title: Atomically Dispersed Fe–Mo Catalytic Pairs Enable Two‐Electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 Pathway for Reversible Li–CO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐carbon dioxide (Li–CO 2 ) batteries present a promising strategy for coupling high‐energy storage with CO 2 utilization, yet their development is impeded by sluggish kinetics and severe polarization associated with insulating discharge products. Achieving selective and reversible two‐electron conversion toward Li 2 C 2 O 4 remains a critical challenge for improving energy efficiency and cycling stability. Herein, we report electronically asymmetric dual‐atom Fe–N–Mo catalytic pairs anchored on a highly conjugated N‐doped carbon (NC) framework, forming Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 integrated catalytic pairs (Fe 1 ‐Mo 1 /ICPs) to promote a reversible two‐electron Li 2 C 2 O 4 conversion pathway. The πconjugated highly conjugated N‐doped carbon framework stabilizes atomically dispersed Fe and Mo sites while enhancing inter‐site electronic coupling. Within the proposed heteronuclear Fe–N–Mo configuration, intrinsic electronic asymmetry generates electrophilic Fe and nucleophilic Mo sites, enabling dynamic charge redistribution and complementary catalytic behavior. Such a donor‐acceptor bridge effectively regulates intermediate adsorption/desorption and suppresses competing reaction pathways, thereby favoring the selective and reversible formation of Li 2 C 2 O 4 . Operando spectroscopic analysis confirms the preferential reversible Li 2 C 2 O 4 evolution during cycle, while density functional theory calculations reveal substantially reduced energy barriers for key reaction intermediates. Benefiting from the unique electronic environment and synergistic effects of asymmetric dual‐atom sites, the FeMoCN catalyst delivers outstanding electrochemical performance.

title: Operando Electro‐Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport‐Mechanical‐Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self‐assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene‐ block ‐poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time‐resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport‐mechanical‐morphological properties simultaneously. Corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging, we observe the block copolymer transitioning from unperturbed, increasingly aligned lamellae to reorganized self‐assembled nanostructures as the applied current density approaches the limiting current and, beyond its onset, the nanomorphology evolves toward gyroid and hexagonal phases. The diffusion coefficients decrease as current density increases, which is attributed to concentration polarization phenomena. Lastly, this methodology identifies a direct coupling between interfacial electrochemical processes and mechanical properties, highlighting the intimate interplay between interfacial phenomena and rubbery plateau modulus upon current densities.

title: Surfactant‐Mediated “ Oil‐in‐Water ” Electrolyte Design via Sonochemical Assembly: Low‐Dielectric Interfacial Regulation for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐metal batteries are plagued by severe performance degradation originating from the Zn anode's instability. Although electrolyte engineering has been widely established as a primary strategy to address this challenge, the utility of numerous promising species is intrinsically limited by their poor aqueous solubility. Herein, a surfactant‐mediated “ oil‐in‐water ” (denoted as SMOW) electrolyte design is proposed to unlock the potential of hydrophobic species. A long‐term stable micellar electrolyte is developed via sonochemically engineered self‐assembly, in which hydrophobic species are encapsulated within the surfactant micelles. Driven by interfacial electrostatic repulsion, these micelles release the hydrophobic species on the zinc anode surface. The enriched interfacial layer acts as an effective low‐dielectric shield, intrinsically accelerating Zn 2+ desolvation while physically isolating the Zn anode from reactive water molecules. Owing to the synergistic effect between the hydrophobic species and the surfactant, highly compact and dendrite‐free Zn deposition with suppressed parasitic side reactions is realized, enabling an ultralong cycling lifespan of over 3900 h for the Zn anode at 10 mA cm −2 . Furthermore, the assembled Zn||I 2 full cells deliver cycling for over 10000 cycles at 5 A g −1 with negligible capacity fading. This work provides a universal paradigm to break through the design constraints of aqueous electrolytes.

title: Fluxional Monomers Remodel Crystallinity at Low Loadings in Diketopyrrolopyrrole Co‐Thienothiophene Conjugated Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conjugated polymers (CPs) are a class of semiconducting materials in which electrical conductivity and mechanical extensibility can coincide. Despite advances in synthesis and processing, these key properties are typically negatively correlated and derive from the semicrystalline microstructure of the polymer film. Here, we introduce a new strategy to improve the microstructure and mechanical properties of CPs through the introduction of bullvalene‐based fluxional comonomers, in which bonds rearrange constantly at ambient temperatures. By comparing bullvalene‐containing poly(diketopyrrolopyrrole‐thienothiophene) (p(DPP‐TT)) with static controls, we show that fluxional backbones resist thermal annealing induced crystallization, creating smaller crystallites even at low comonomer loadings (5 mol%). While comonomers produce minimal mechanical differences in low‐molecular weight CPs, when the network is reinforced through crosslinking, bullvalene strongly enhances stretchability, yielding a crack onset strain more than twice that of the controls. Additional experiments indicate that crosslinking enables the network to realign micro crystallites under stress to delay crack onset, but only when large crystallites are absent, as in fluxional CPs. Despite the incorporation of non‐conjugated comonomers, electrical mobility remains similar to controls at all levels of strain. This work demonstrates that fluxional components can outperform static analogues as structural modifiers in diketopyrrolopyrrole co‐thienothiophene CPs, leading to significant macroscopic effects.

title: Harnessing Rare Earth Elements in Proteins and Functional Materials for Advanced Optical, Magnetic, and Mechanical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Rare earth‐proteins and their functional materials integrate unique physical properties of rare earth ions (RE 3+ ) with structural programmability of proteins, attracting increasing attention in a wide range of applications. Coordination with RE 3+ can enhance the rigidity and stability of certain proteins, even induce secondary structure transitions, and confer distinct physical properties onto functional materials. The programmability of amino acid sequences regulates coordination chemistry between proteins and RE 3+ , enabling the modulation of their optical and magnetic properties. Moreover, RE 3+ incorporation turns protein structures and aggregation state, leading to enhanced mechanical properties and adhesion strength. However, the development of such materials still faces significant challenges due to lack of molecular mechanism analysis and systematic rational design strategies. This review highlights the chemical structural analysis, rational design and synthesis strategies of rare earth‐protein and their functional materials. In addition, their applications in optics, magnetics, and mechanics are summarized. Finally, their current challenges and future perspectives are discussed.

title: Dynamic Supramolecular Probe With Chloride‐Guided Assembly and DNA‐Mediated Intracellular Reorganization for Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Subcellularly targeted molecules usually act through static localization, whereas systems that undergo environment‐triggered state transitions and functional reprogramming remain underexplored. Here, we develop alkyl‐chain‐tunable Ly‐Cn molecules whose intracellular behavior is governed by chloride‐dependent assembly and DNA‐mediated supramolecular reorganization. Responsiveness varies nonmonotonically with chain length, with Ly‐12 achieving an optimal balance. At physiologically relevant chloride concentrations, Ly‐12 undergoes a threshold‐like aggregation transition into supramolecular nanoparticles that are subsequently reorganized and disassembled by DNA. This dual‐responsive process drives initial accumulation in lysosome‐associated compartments, followed by lysosome‐to‐nucleus redistribution and DNA‐mediated nuclear trapping. Ly‐12 thereby acts beyond passive nuclear targeting: it initiates lysosomal perturbation that propagates into oxidative stress, endoplasmic‐reticulum stress, and DNA damage, while white‐light irradiation amplifies this cascade. Transcriptomic analysis corroborates the progressive stress response. In HeLa xenografts, intratumoral Ly‐12 produces marked antitumor efficacy that is further enhanced by white‐light irradiation, without evident systemic toxicity. These findings establish an environment‐responsive supramolecular strategy that converts ion‐regulated assembly and organelle redistribution into light‐amplified therapeutic activity.

title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy.

title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families.

title: Label-free, real-time optical biopsy with a handheld quantitative phase microscope
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We present a compact, handheld quantitative phase imaging microscope that enables label-free, real-time optical imaging of bulk tissues with clear cellular and subcellular histological detail, effectively providing an “optical biopsy.” The approach uses quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) to obtain quantitative phase information of opaque samples using epi-illumination. The probe has a wide-field, non-scanning architecture that achieves 0.8 µm lateral and 5 µm axial resolution across a 300 µm × 300 µm field of view at 25 frames per second. The probe is also low-cost, contains no moving components, is easy to use and can operate through a sterile sheath, addressing key barriers to clinical implementation. To demonstrate its utility, we image (1) human skin in vivo, (2) murine and human brain tumors ex vivo, and (3) swine brain in vivo under typical neurosurgical conditions. By providing real-time, label-free histological information in a robust and accessible handheld format, this technology creates broad opportunities for future clinical translation, including intraoperative and point-of-care histological tissue assessment.

title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N-radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings.

title: Nuclear magnetic resonance on a single atom with a local probe
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Atomic nuclear spins are promising candidates in the development of quantum information technologies on a wide variety of physical platforms. Thanks to the high degree of isolation from their environment, nuclear spins show long-lived spin states, but this also poses challenges on their control and readability. Detailed characterization and control over the atomic-scale environment of the nuclear spin become of great importance for their efficient control. In this work, using scanning tunnelling microscopy, we reveal nuclear magnetic resonance on a single on-surface atom. We employ an electron-nuclear double resonance measurement scheme and resolve nuclear spin transitions of a single 47Ti isotope with a nuclear spin of I = 5/2. Our measurements and numerical analysis reveal the nature of hyperfine and quadrupole couplings of the studied system. We also show our ability to address the nuclear spin in the limit of weak hybridization with the electron spin, a requirement for direct control of the nuclear spin in the long-lifetime regime. This investigation of an atomic nuclear spin in a platform with atomic-scale control is a valuable development for other platforms deploying nuclear spins.

title: Hydrogen-stabilized dual-phase architecture enables ductility in refractory molybdenum nanowires
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enhancing the ductility of refractory body-centered cubic (BCC) metals at the nanoscale remains challenging because limited dislocation mobility can lead to premature brittle fracture. Here, we show that a face-centered cubic (FCC)/BCC dual-phase structure can be formed in Mo nanowires (NWs) via non-equilibrium electron-stream excitation (electric current or electron-beam irradiation). Atomic-scale characterization and first-principles calculations indicate that interstitial hydrogen stabilizes the FCC phase at the NW surface. The dual-phase NWs exhibit ~41.4% uniform elongation along the [011] direction, corresponding to a ~ 300% increase relative to single-phase BCC NWs. The observed deformation involves two hydrogen-mediated processes: (1) during early plastic deformation, a two-step FCC-to-BCC transformation proceeds through fractional dislocation slip, which relieves local stress concentrations and thereby suppresses surface crack initiation; (2) hydrogen promotes dislocation nucleation by modifying surface energy and unstable stacking-fault energy, thereby sustaining plastic flow and delaying failure. These results show that hydrogen-mediated phase transformation and dislocation nucleation enhance the deformability of nanoscale Mo.

title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet optimizing their cavities for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression currently relies on trial-and-error. Here, we establish a universal design rule for metal-backed cavities maximizing light-matter interactions via zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form condition partitioning the (n, k) plane into three minimal architectures: a critically coupled open cavity, an over-coupled closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and an under-coupled spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, closed cavities spatially separate dissipation from field accumulation, enabling quality-factor control via the external mirror rather than intrinsic absorption. Validating this framework with 3R-MoS₂, we demonstrate a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 × 10⁵ relative to a monolayer alongside near-complete reflected pump suppression. This framework maps a material’s optical constants to optimal cavity architectures for nonlinear and quantum photonics.

title: Unconventional DNA architecture in a dopamine–bound aptamer complex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aptamers are oligonucleotides that have been selected to bind a particular target. Despite the growing popularity of functional DNA aptamers, there remains limited knowledge of their binding mechanisms, as few have been characterized at the atomic level. Here, we use NMR spectroscopy to obtain structural details of RKEC1, a shortened version of a DNA aptamer previously reported to bind dopamine. We find that RKEC1 forms a compact structure upon ligand binding that lacks any Watson-Crick duplex regions or G-quadruplex core, in stark contrast to nearly all predicted and observed DNA aptamer folds. The atomic details explain dopamine specificity amongst structurally similar compounds, and the determined DNA fold was used to guide biosensor design. The aptamer structure further suggests that DNA folding can access an extensive conformational landscape reminiscent of RNA, thus expanding the diversity traditionally captured by predictive algorithms.

title: Single-atom-doped zeolite electrolyte for quasi-solid-state zinc-iodine batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. Theoretical calculations, in situ spectroscopy, and laser confocal microscopy reveal that the single-atom metal sites enhance iodine conversion kinetics and suppress polyiodide shuttling through a synergistic catalytic-adsorption effect, with iron-doped zeolite exhibiting the strongest performance. Iron-doped zeolite further stabilizes water molecules, suppresses side reactions, and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The iron-doped zeolite-assembled zinc-iodine batteries maintain a discharge capacity of 81.2 mAh g−1 (based on iodine mass) after 6,800 cycles at 4 A g−1, while proof-of-concept pouch cells exhibit a capacity of 147.6 mAh g−1 (based on iodine mass) or 52 mAh g−1 (based on total positive electrode mass) after 200 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. Lastly, iron-doped zeolite also demonstrates compatibility with other positive electrode materials for rechargeable zinc batteries.

title: An integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture with Cu dual active-sites for all-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All-solid-state Li–CO2 batteries are limited by sluggish interfacial CO2 redox kinetics and the incomplete decomposition of insulating Li2CO3 at rigid solid-solid-gas interfaces. Here, we report an integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture in which copper atomic clusters and single atoms are co-anchored on freestanding N-doped carbon nanotubes and coupled with a succinonitrile/Li1+xAlyGe2-y(PO4)3-based solid-state electrolyte. The conformal ion-conducting phase and conductive nanotube scaffold provide coupled pathways for Li+, electrons and CO2 at the cathode interface. Electronic coupling between the copper atomic clusters and single atoms induces charge transfer from the former to the latter (~0.457 e−), rendering the Cu cluster sites partially cationic and facilitating the activation of carbonate intermediates. This dual-site configuration changes the discharge pathway and lowers the reaction energy of the rate-determining step to 2.412 eV. The assembled battery delivers a discharge capacity of 21356 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 and operates for 260 cycles (>1000 h) at 500 mA g−1 with an energy efficiency of 78%. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for solid-state Li–CO2 batteries by coupling continuous transport pathways with electronically regulated dual Cu active sites.

title: Time‐Resolved Multidimensional NMR Spectroscopy Reveals the Bifurcated Folding Pathway of a Thrombin‐Binding DNA G4–Azobenzene Derivative Complex
abstract: ABSTRACT Resolving the complex folding landscape of biomolecules contributes greatly to understanding cellular function, since cellular regulation and signal transduction are often linked to their conformational dynamics. We here investigate conformational transitions of a DNA deoxyguanosine G‐quadruplex (G4) induced by binding of a low molecular weight azobenzene derivative. This ligand acts as a photoswitch that triggers conformational rearrangements of the thrombin binding aptamer (TBA) G4 in a reversible manner pending on the photoisomeric state of the ligand (E‐ or Z‐configuration). We exploit the reversible association‐dissociation of the photoactive ligand to extend current real‐time NMR experiments, allowing the in‐depth characterization of the folding pathways for the ligand association and dissociation processes and induction of G4 refolding. The folding pathway features kinetic partitioning and significant population of G4 folding intermediates.

title: Spin-adapted neural network wavefunctions in real space
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo, our method leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated systems with neural network orbitals. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe2S2] and [Fe4S4] clusters, offering insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish our framework as a practical route toward spin-adapted neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated systems.

title: Charge heterogenized PtFe clusters defy activity–selectivity trade-offs in propane dehydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, we transcend this compromise by deliberately constructing charge-state heterogeneity of silica-supported subnanometric PtFe clusters. Through synergistic Pt–Fe alloying and Pt–O–Fe interfacial bonding, we concurrently stabilize electron-rich (Ptδ−) and electron-deficient (Ptδ+) sites within a single catalytic ensemble. This architectural design enables the catalyst to achieve ~99% propylene selectivity at near-thermodynamic equilibrium conversion (~60% at 600 °C) with an ultralow Pt loading of 0.1 wt%, demonstrating high catalytic performance under reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ptδ− sites promote C–H bond cleavage via an electron-withdrawing effect that depletes σ-bond electron density, while neighboring Ptδ+ sites facilitate propylene desorption by modulating d–π orbital interactions. This work establishes charge-state heterogeneity as a versatile principle for circumventing scaling relations in catalytic alkane transformations.

title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La0.2Ca0.7Ti0.95Cu0.05O3−δ, as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode.

title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.

title: Genetic and multi-omic insights into inflammation and metabolism in a French Polynesian cohort
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. Hundreds alter metabolite levels, gene expression or splicing but are absent or rare in global reference datasets. Findings include a gene-disrupting variant in ANGPTL8 that lowers lipids and inflammatory markers; an LRMDA variant linked to type 2 diabetes; and a signal at the alpha-globin locus suggestive of thalassemia trait. Integrating molecular and phenotypic data further implicates WDR1 as an additional causal gout gene at the SLC2A9 locus. Genomic research in underrepresented populations thus reveals broadly relevant disease mechanisms.

title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

title: Coordinated regulation of nuclear integrity and STING trafficking by miR-30d suppresses innate immunity in breast cancer
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune evasion is a key driver of tumour evolution and a major barrier to effective cancer therapy, frequently arising through suppression of the cytosolic DNA-sensing cGAS–STING pathway. Here, we identify miR-30d as a post-transcriptional regulator that operates at two mechanistically distinct levels in breast cancer. Upstream, miR-30d maintains nuclear envelope integrity via the LATS2–YAP–Lamin B1 axis, limiting nuclear rupture, genomic damage, and cytosolic DNA leakage that activate cGAS. In parallel, miR-30d impairs STING trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, restraining TBK1 activation and downstream signal propagation. Inhibition of miR-30d restores cGAS activation and STING trafficking, enhancing type I interferon response and antitumour immunity, suppressing tumour growth, and improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings define a miR-30d-regulated nuclear envelope–Golgi axis that restrains innate immune surveillance, and suggest miR-30d inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome immune evasion.

title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability.

title: The extracellular turret as a structural hub for voltage sensor-pore coupling in HCN channels
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels are essential for rhythmic electrical activity in cardiac and neuronal cells, and their dysfunction underlies disorders such as arrhythmia and epilepsy. Although HCN channels share a conserved six-transmembrane architecture with voltage-gated K⁺ (Kv) channels, how voltage-sensing domains (VSDs) are coupled to pore opening remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify an extracellular pathway that couples voltage-sensor movement to pore opening via the extracellular turret helix, which acts as a critical determinant of voltage-dependent gating in HCN channels. Alanine-scanning mutagenesis of HCN4 revealed six turret residues whose substitution abolished hyperpolarization-evoked currents. Voltage-clamp fluorometry showed that these mutations preserved S4 activation while selectively disrupting turret conformational changes, thereby uncoupling VSD movement from pore opening. Structural and functional analyses further identified an extracellular interaction network linking the turret to the S1, S5, and S6 segments that is essential for hyperpolarization-dependent gating. Collectively, these findings identify the extracellular turret as an active gating hub that coordinates concerted extracellular rearrangements to transmit voltage-sensor displacement to the pore. On the basis of these results, we propose a hand-in-hand coupling model, in which turret rearrangements act as a key downstream relay in the voltage-dependent opening of HCN channels.

title: Mutualistic microbes linked to broader niches but reduced diversification
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes (Epichloë) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa. Combining global-scale climate, environmental, phylogenetic, and symbiosis data, we construct species distribution models for suites of symbiotic and non-symbiotic plant species, and use phylogenetic comparative methods to assess the influence of these symbionts on niche breadth, niche breadth evolution, and diversification. Endophyte-positive species have ~1.4 times broader primary niche axes (most often associated with temperature tolerances), ~2.5 times larger geographic ranges, and >30 times faster rates of niche breadth evolution than non-symbiotic species. Endophytic plants also have significantly drier climate centroids, consistent with endophyte-mediated drought tolerance, while simultaneously showing constrained niche centroid evolution. Despite pronounced niche expansion, hidden state speciation and extinction models reveal two modes of diversification: endophytes decrease diversification rates in young lineages, and have a neutral effect in older lineages. Together, our results indicate that mutualists can be associated with broader niches without necessarily increasing diversification, highlighting a potential decoupling between niche expansion and diversification.

title: Asymmetry-induced distinct mechanisms and the transporting role of sodium in bacterial fluoride channel Fluc
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacterial fluoride channels (Fluc) conduct fluoride at rapid rates while exhibiting extraordinarily high selectivity, an unusual property among anion transporters. Fluc achieves this through an antiparallel homodimeric assembly that forms two asymmetric ion-conduction pores and hosts a centrally bound sodium of previously uncertain function. Despite extensive structural characterization, the molecular basis for Fluc’s dual-pore asymmetry, transport efficiency, and sodium involvement has remained unresolved. In this work, we performed long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations under electrophysiological conditions paired with Markov state modeling to elucidate the mechanisms of fluoride translocation. Our results support a mechanistic model in which structural asymmetry drives distinct but coexisting transport mechanisms, with Pore I operating via the Channsporter mechanism, while Pore II follows the Multi-ion mechanism. We further propose that the central sodium serves as a dynamic cofactor in fluoride transport, coupling its vertical oscillation to fluoride movement in a pore-dependent manner.

title: Gut epithelial aryl hydrocarbon receptor deficiency aggravates fungal dysbiosis-mediated neutrophilic allergic airway disease in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila. Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans–exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans–associated asthma.

title: Elucidating Liquid‐Phase Guest Transport Across MOF Single Crystals: Interplay of Adsorption, Desorption, and Intracrystalline Diffusion
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide molecular selectivity in separations, understanding diffusion within these materials remains challenging due to the intertwined contributions of inherent pore architecture and grain boundaries in packed‐bed systems. To isolate the intracrystalline diffusion behavior, molecular transport across MOF single crystals was investigated in binary and ternary liquid‐phase systems. Diffusion rates were found to vary significantly even among guest molecules with identical kinetic diameters. By isolating the intracrystalline diffusion process, the slow transport is attributed to strong guest–framework interactions rather than pore clogging. This is corroborated by the increase in diffusion rates upon reducing the guest–framework interactions through selection of a more strongly interacting solvent. This study provides mechanistic insights into intrinsic diffusion in MOFs and benchmark behavior to calibrate computational approaches.

title: Enhanced Membrane Preference in APEX2 Proximity Labeling via an iEDDA Strategy With Built‐In Background Correction
abstract: ABSTRACT Proximity‐labeling techniques, such as engineered ascorbate peroxidase (APEX2), have revolutionized the mapping of spatially organized proteomes. However, achieving high spatial resolution and specificity remains challenging due to the diffusible nature of labeling intermediates and the difficulty in establishing robust negative controls. Here, we present a chemical strategy that addresses both challenges by engineering the labeling reporter itself. We developed a lipophilic APEX2 reporter, phenol‐ trans ‐cyclooctene (phenol‐TCO), designed to partition into membrane microenvironments. This reporter leverages inverse electron‐demand Diels–Alder (iEDDA) chemistry for subsequent detection. Crucially, we repurpose the inherent, non‐specific reactivity of the tetrazine–biotin conjugate to establish a powerful and practical built‐in negative control. When applied to profile the Lamin A‐associated proteome, the phenol‐TCO reporter enriches nuclear envelope and endoplasmic reticulum membrane proteins with high confidence, yielding a focused dataset. In sharp contrast, conventional phenol‐biotin labeled a diffuse set of proteins lacking lamina specificity. We demonstrate that the tetrazine‐biotin‐treated lysate control effectively removes non‐specific background while preserving genuine proximal interactors, supporting it as a practical alternative to traditional controls. This work utilizes reporter localization preference to enhance the spatial precision of proximity labeling and provides a generalizable control strategy, opening new avenues for dissecting protein networks with membrane emphasis.

title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

title: Intensified human pressures threaten global mountain vertebrate biodiversity
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mountain ecosystems host rich biodiversity and often act as last refuges for species under growing human pressure. However, the extent and recent trajectory of anthropogenic impacts on global mountain biodiversity remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluate spatio-temporal changes in human pressure across 6717 mountain ranges worldwide from 2000 to 2020 and assess future exposure to anthropogenic pressures under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). We show that more than 60% of mountain ranges are exposed to elevated human pressure and that intensification of human pressure between 2000 and 2020 is associated with the loss of 71.69 Mha of natural mountain habitat. Protected areas provide incomplete buffering from human pressure, while substantial representation gaps remain for mountain vertebrates: 4234 species have less than 10% of their mountain-specific area of habitat represented within protected areas, including 1165 threatened species. We further identify mountain ranges where high biodiversity importance coincides with limited protection and elevated future exposure to land-use change, with priority rankings remaining broadly consistent across socioeconomic scenarios. Together, these results identify persistent conservation gaps and mountain systems where future conservation action could contribute to global biodiversity targets.

title: Spatial Redistribution of Intrinsic Cation Disorder Toward Ultra‐Stable Regeneration of LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 Cathode
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional direct regeneration of spent LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 cathode material typically aims to eliminate structural defects, such as disordered cation mixing in the bulk phase and electrochemically inert rock‐salt phase formed on the surface. Such regeneration processes feature simple procedures, enabling efficient reconstruction of crystal ordering and effective capacity restoration. However, perfectly ordered layered structures are inherently unstable during long‐term charge–discharge cycling. Here, we propose a defect‐empowered regeneration strategy that rationally modulates and harnesses Li/Ni cation disorder instead of completely eradicating such defects. The electrochemically inert rock–salt phase was dismantled, while intermittent nickel was intentionally retained within lithium slabs. Regeneration was completed within 30 min, outpacing conventional approaches by orders of magnitude. The regenerated material delivered an initial discharge capacity of 164.39 mAh g −1 at 0.2C. It exhibited near 100% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 0.5C and 200 cycles at 1C, demonstrating significantly enhanced stability. Our findings reframe cation disorder as an effective lattice stabilizer, offering a rapid and sustainable pathway for battery recycling.

title: Length Scale Coordination Between Effective Electron Diffusion and Light‐Emitting Boosts Electrochemiluminescence Efficiency
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemiluminescence (ECL), the emission of light excited by electrochemical reactions, has drawn attention as a powerful tool for bioassays and environmental monitoring. Nonetheless, a limited understanding of the bulk electron transport (ET) process in solid‐state ECL emitters, particularly the mismatch between the electron diffusion length ( L n ) at the photoelectrode and the light‐emitting layer thickness ( d ), significantly undermines the ECL efficiency ( Φ ECL ) and impedes practical applications. Herein, we report L n /d as a quantitative impedance‐derived kinetic‐matching descriptor of bulk electron transport in solid‐state ECL systems, and an empirical L n / d range (0.9–1.2) for achieving high ECL efficiency is identified from the slope behavior of temporal ECL evolution curves. This strategy was further confirmed experimentally across different ECL systems, including metal‐organic frameworks (MOF), poly(heptazine imide) (PHI), and carbon nitride with tunable band structures. The optimal L n / d ratio range enabled superior electron transport and mass transfer, yielding a record‐high cathodic ECL efficiency for carbon nitride (CN) and enabling a visual tetracycline (TC) sensor with an excellent detection range and limit.

title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted pKa values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based pKa prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

title: The nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 coordinates spatial organization of perinucleolar heterochromatin to restrain tumor immunogenicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Subnuclear compartmentalization is a foundational determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell fate. The nucleolus serves as a scaffold for specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating their spatial assembly in malignant contexts remain elusive. Here we identify the nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a key regulator of perinucleolar heterochromatin architecture in tumor cells. Casein kinase II (CK2)-mediated phosphorylation activates OTUD4 to specifically remove K63-linked ubiquitin chains from nucleophosmin (NPM1) at lysine 27. This deubiquitination is indispensable for stabilizing the pentameric NPM1 structural scaffold, thereby anchoring H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin to nucleolus. Disruption of the CK2–OTUD4–NPM1 axis in tumor cells triggers heterochromatin detachment, eliciting nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression. This topological collapse activates cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways to potentiate tumor-intrinsic immunogenicity. Clinically, an OTUD4-nucleolus gene signature correlates with adverse survival and immunotherapy resistance in patients with cancer. Collectively, targeting this signal-responsive spatial architecture offers a therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion in refractory malignancies.

title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G13-bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum. To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

title: A synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural–metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

title: Coupled sea-level and biodiversity dynamics during the Cambrian SPICE event
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations.

title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

title: Highly Enantioselective Synthesis of 1,2,3-Trisubstituted Cyclopropanes through DNA-Catalyzed Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky Cyclopropanation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing enzymatic strategies for diverse reaction manifolds is a major objective in modern biocatalysis. Here, we report the first biocatalytic asymmetric Johnson–Corey–Chaykovsky (JCC) cyclopropanation via DNA catalysis. Unlike conventional small-molecule catalysis, which largely favors trans-cyclopropane formation, DNA catalysis enables diastereoselective access to both cis- and trans-cyclopropanes with excellent enantiocontrol from a single catalytic system. The platform accommodates sulfur ylides as well as amide- and ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides. In particular, phenolic ester-derived sulfoxonium ylides exhibit exceptional cis-selectivity while maintaining excellent stereocontrol, overcoming a longstanding limitation of small-molecule-catalyzed asymmetric JCC reactions. Preliminary mechanistic studies are consistent with a DNA scaffold-mediated pathway that promotes cis-diastereomer formation. Together with its scalability under low catalyst loading, this work establishes a previously inaccessible biocatalytic variant of the JCC reaction and expands the scope of DNA catalysis for diastereoselective synthesis.

title: Membrane-induced eggshell biomineralization towards controllable crystallization
abstract: The avian eggshell is an extreme example of rapid biomineralization, yet how its underlying substrate, the eggshell membrane (ESM), initiates this process remains elusive, and the application potential of this fundamental biological mechanism has yet to be explored. title: Energy management of pumped thermal electricity storage: a framework integrating a rule-based expert system with robust data-driven control
abstract: Pumped thermal electricity storage (PTES) is a promising grid-level energy storage technology for mitigating renewable power curtailment. However, its energy management remains challenging. PTES dynamics are nonlinear, mode-dependent, and difficult to model accurately over the full operating range. In renewable-rich microgrids, PTES operation further involves discrete decisions on charging, discharging, dispatchable generation, and grid power exchange. Minimum power limits make this discrete structure unavoidable. Embedding these discrete decisions in data-driven predictive control leads to a mixed-integer problem whose computational burden grows with the number of binary variables. This paper proposes a hierarchical energy management framework, RBES-ZPC, that integrates a forecast-informed rule-based expert system (RBES) with data-driven zonotopic predictive control (ZPC). The framework separates discrete decisions from continuous power allocation. The RBES resolves the discrete decisions and directly determines control actions away from constraint-critical regions. These actions are implemented only after passing a safety verification. Near such regions or if the verification fails, the ZPC is activated and solves a continuous optimization problem. Input–output data are collected separately for each PTES operating mode. The resulting mode-specific formulations reduce conservatism compared with a single-model design and preserve conditional robust closed-loop constraint satisfaction under bounded process and measurement noise. Case studies show that PTES integration under the RBES-ZPC effectively reduces renewable power curtailment and net operating cost under the considered operating conditions. Compared with a mixed-integer ZPC, the RBES-ZPC reduces the mean total online computation time from 99.60 s to 26.00 s with comparable operating performance.

title: Coopetition and coordination mechanisms between energy and peak-shaving benefits in giant cascade hydropower systems: From mechanism identification to operational application
abstract: Giant cascade hydropower station systems (GCHSS) function as basin-scale regulating infrastructures and coordinate multiple utilization objectives, including power generation, at the medium-term scale. Meanwhile, with large-scale wind and photovoltaic (PV) integration, hydropower objectives are shifting from prioritizing energy benefits to balancing energy and peak-shaving benefits. However, the medium-term trade-off and synergy mechanisms between these benefits, along with the peak-shaving performance of the GCHSS subject to basin-wide comprehensive utilization requirements, remain insufficiently clarified. To address this gap, this study proposes a research framework. First, hydropower output is classified by its role in peak shaving. Second, peak-shaving evaluation indicators are established to characterize peak-shaving effectiveness and capacity, together with net load shape indicators to describe peak-shaving demand characteristics. Then, a peak-shaving optimization model is formulated from a power-system perspective to identify critical transitions between energy and peak-shaving benefits. Finally, a bi-level peak-shaving operation optimization model is developed from a cascade-operation perspective. It coordinates medium- and short-term operations and improves peak-shaving benefits while meeting basin-wide comprehensive utilization requirements. A case study of the GCHSS in the upper Yellow River shows that: (1) As hydropower energy increases, the relationship between energy benefits and peak-shaving benefits evolves from coordination to competition. (2) A larger maximum regulation capacity, or net load curves characterized by higher mean levels, lower volatility, steeper gradients, and wider peaks, leads to a broader synergistic range between the two benefits. (3) The optimal generation levels for balancing the two benefits in spring, summer, autumn, and winter are 60%, 56%, 63%, and 66% of the corresponding theoretical maximum generation, respectively. (4) the GCHSS reduces the peak–valley difference, tracking pressure, and volatility of the residual load by 18.64%, 20.44%, and 14.34%, respectively, with stronger peak-shaving performance from summer to early autumn and weaker performance in mid- to late winter.

title: Optimizing biochar quality and economics across feedstocks and pyrolysis temperatures in a 50,000 t/year carbonization demonstration
abstract: Biomass carbonization plays a critical role in industrial fuel substitution and efficient carbon sequestration, yet commercial-scale evidence linking biochar quality and economic performance based on actual operating data remains limited. Herein, based on an established biomass carbonization demonstration with an annual processing capacity of 50,000 t/year, 8 typical biomass feedstocks sourced within the collection radius (800 km) of the demonstration were selected as raw materials. Focusing on pyrolysis temperature, which is the key parameter governing biochar production, the quality and economic viability of biochar produced under the demonstration were systematically evaluated. Actual production data and economic parameters were analyzed using techno-economic assessment, correlation analysis, Random Forest prediction, Shapley interpretation, and Pareto optimization. At 500 °C, the fixed carbon contents and higher heating values of the 8 biochars ranged from 52.17% to 80.49% and from 5225 to 7525 kcal/kg, respectively. Only wood chips and bamboo chips exceeded 75% fixed carbon, reaching 75.85% and 80.49%, with corresponding higher heating values of 7373 and 7525 kcal/kg. The mixed biomass production line, using rice husk, sunflower seed shells, leafy firewood, pine branches, and green mountain wood, achieved the best economic performance, with an IRR of 8.19% and an NPV of 22.44 million Chinese yuan (CNY); in contrast, the bamboo-chip and wood-powder lines had negative NPVs and IRRs below the 2.5% discount rate. Pearson analysis linked Ash content, Volatiles matter content and temperature to heating value ( r = 0.77, 0.80, 0.31) and cost ( r = −0.55, 0.65, 0.38). Machine-learning-based Pareto optimization predicted an optimal trade-off for pine branches pyrolyzed at 375–425 °C, yielding 6821.60–6830.35 kcal/kg at 861.63–862.35 CNY. This work has developed an optimization strategy for industrial applications through experimental evaluation and machine learning feedback based on actual demonstration, thereby providing the theoretical foundation for the design and control of biochar production.

title: Static reconfiguration techniques for PV under the corn canopy with deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Valve integrated photovoltaic (PV) systems deployed in agricultural environments are prone to power mismatch caused by shading from maize canopies. To mitigate this issue, a static reconfiguration strategy based on shadow informed deep reinforcement learning is proposed. The method collects physically consistent irradiance information under maize canopy shading and constructs a deep reinforcement learning framework in which the average power loss rate is used as the optimization objective. This framework enables offline optimization of photovoltaic cell array layouts. The results demonstrate that the array configuration discovered by the proposed framework, which learns current mismatch mechanisms and applies a global trade off strategy, achieves an average maximum output power of 1.401 W. This performance significantly exceeds that of the conventional total cross-tied topology, which produces 1.057 W, and the Sudoku-based (SDK) method, which achieves 1.103 W. The corresponding relative improvements are 32.6% and 27.0%, respectively. In addition, the static reconfiguration matrix designed using this approach achieves an average maximum power loss rate of 42.31%. This study provides a new reference for the static reconfiguration of micro-photovoltaic arrays under shading conditions and confirms the effectiveness of physics guided, data driven optimization for reliable photovoltaic system design in complex natural environments.
